eval.title: Berkshire BRK Stock Analysis 2H 2025

call.headline_quote: This might be blasphemy but I don't think Birkshshire is such a great buy nor a hold at the moment. Perhaps a hold.

base_metric.name: net_income
base_metric.quote: 17 billion for the first 6 months, 17 billion for the next 6 months and that's 34 billion of value creation from Birkshshire

scenarios.name: normal
scenarios.quote: for a discount rate or expected return of 10% the intrinsic value is 390 billion

scenarios.name: worst
scenarios.quote: bad case scenario let's say a downturn or recession or something birkshshireare goes 70% down from where it is now

what_is_priced_in.quote: market capitalization of Burkshshire is expected to be 1 trillion in 2034

reasons.claim: At a $1 trillion market cap versus his $390 billion intrinsic value, Berkshire is expensive from an intrinsic value perspective.
reasons.quote: if I compare my 300 billion with the market cap of 1 trillion ion. It's really really a bad situation from an intrinsic value perspective.

data_check.gap_note: he says 390, as-of 3.52129e+11 (T0); annual vs TTM or a different definition

reasons.claim: Buffett's huge, growing cash pile signals he sees nothing worth buying, implying markets and Berkshire itself are expensive.
reasons.quote: This is his cash pile. Therefore, he is saying, "Look guys, there is nothing to buy. This is extremely expensive the markets. I'm not buying anything."

data_check.gap_note: he says 3.44e+11, as-of 4.8376e+10 (FY2024); annual vs TTM or a different definition

reasons.claim: Buffett's own buyback behavior—buying heavily when the price was half or 40% of today's level and now stopping—signals the stock is not cheap now.
reasons.quote: he was doing buybacks here when the price was half of what is now 40% of what it is now. Here he isn't doing it buyback. So I cannot tell you okay it is a great buy.

data_check.gap_note: trajectory visible at T0; no number stated

reasons.claim: Berkshire's enormous size ($340 billion cash) limits its ability to deploy capital effectively, capping long-term returns.
reasons.quote: the issue with Berkshire is of course its size because 340 billion of cash that's not something you can deploy like this

data_check.gap_note: he says 3.4e+11, as-of 4.8376e+10 (FY2024); annual vs TTM or a different definition

reasons.claim: Even with a modest ~4-7% return estimate, Berkshire remains a reliable long-term wealth compounding machine that will outperform most alternatives.
reasons.quote: Berkshire is an okay long-term always will be always is an okay long-term wealth compounding machine. If you buy Berkshire now and you leave it there for the next 30, 40 years, I'm very sure that it will do very good, much better than 98% of other things.

data_check.gap_note: not in our data: value creation return

external_facts_used: Buffett's public statements/promise of 8-10% return on Berkshire through conference calls
3-month treasury yield of 3.54% used to estimate interest income on cash
Berkshire's buyback history and prices at which buybacks were made

critic.notes: ok. Borderline: 4-7% expected return and 'bad situation from intrinsic value' lean toward avoid, but his explicit 'perhaps a hold' and 'will do very good over 30-40 years' support fair_hold.
